front_blocks.md: Define **program development life cycle (PDLC)**.

back_blocks.md: The PDLC is a **structured process used to design, build and test software solutions**.

cards.front_md: Define **program development life cycle (PDLC)**.
cards.back_md: The PDLC is a **structured process used to design, build and test software solutions**.

front_blocks.md: What does the program development life cycle ensure?

back_blocks.md: That programs are developed **systematically, efficiently and to a high standard**.

cards.front_md: What does the program development life cycle ensure?
cards.back_md: That programs are developed **systematically, efficiently and to a high standard**.

front_blocks.md: Name the five stages of the program development life cycle.

back_blocks.md: **Analysis**, **design**, **coding**, **testing** and **maintenance**.

cards.front_md: Name the five stages of the program development life cycle.
cards.back_md: **Analysis**, **design**, **coding**, **testing** and **maintenance**.

front_blocks.md: What is the purpose of the analysis stage?

back_blocks.md: To **understand the problem** that the program is being created to solve.

cards.front_md: What is the purpose of the analysis stage?
cards.back_md: To **understand the problem** that the program is being created to solve.

front_blocks.md: How is abstraction used in the analysis stage?

back_blocks.md: To **ignore unnecessary detail** and focus only on what the program **must do** and the **limitations** it must work within.

cards.front_md: How is abstraction used in the analysis stage?
cards.back_md: To **ignore unnecessary detail** and focus only on what the program **must do** and the **limitations** it must work within.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
The analysis stage decides which programming language to use.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
The analysis stage is about **understanding the problem**. The programming language is chosen at the **coding** stage.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

The analysis stage decides which programming language to use.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

The analysis stage is about **understanding the problem**. The programming language is chosen at the **coding** stage.

front_blocks.md: A <u>**                        **</u> document is created during the analysis stage.

back_blocks.md: A **requirements** document is created during the analysis stage.

cards.front_md: A <u>**                        **</u> document is created during the analysis stage.
cards.back_md: A **requirements** document is created during the analysis stage.

front_blocks.md: What does a requirements document do?

back_blocks.md: It **breaks the problem into manageable parts**, **labels each requirement**, and **describes what success looks like** for each feature.

cards.front_md: What does a requirements document do?
cards.back_md: It **breaks the problem into manageable parts**, **labels each requirement**, and **describes what success looks like** for each feature.

front_blocks.md: What happens in the design stage?

back_blocks.md: Developers **plan how the program will work**, creating a **blueprint** for the solution.

cards.front_md: What happens in the design stage?
cards.back_md: Developers **plan how the program will work**, creating a **blueprint** for the solution.

front_blocks.md: Name the three design tools used in the design stage.

back_blocks.md: **Structure diagrams**, **flowcharts** and **pseudocode**.

cards.front_md: Name the three design tools used in the design stage.
cards.back_md: **Structure diagrams**, **flowcharts** and **pseudocode**.

front_blocks.md: What does a structure diagram do?

back_blocks.md: It **breaks the program down into smaller components**.

cards.front_md: What does a structure diagram do?
cards.back_md: It **breaks the program down into smaller components**.

front_blocks.md: What does a flowchart show?

back_blocks.md: The **logical flow of processes**.

cards.front_md: What does a flowchart show?
cards.back_md: The **logical flow of processes**.

front_blocks.md: What happens in the coding stage?

back_blocks.md: Developers write the program in a **suitable programming language**, in **modules** that work together to solve the full problem.

cards.front_md: What happens in the coding stage?
cards.back_md: Developers write the program in a **suitable programming language**, in **modules** that work together to solve the full problem.

front_blocks.md: What is iterative testing in the coding stage?

back_blocks.md: Each module is **tested and debugged individually** as it is created.

cards.front_md: What is iterative testing in the coding stage?
cards.back_md: Each module is **tested and debugged individually** as it is created.

front_blocks.md: Why are modules retested whenever changes are made?

back_blocks.md: To ensure that **no new errors are introduced**.

cards.front_md: Why are modules retested whenever changes are made?
cards.back_md: To ensure that **no new errors are introduced**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Testing is only carried out once the whole program has been written.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
**Iterative testing** happens during the **coding** stage on each module, as well as in the full testing stage once the program is complete.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Testing is only carried out once the whole program has been written.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

**Iterative testing** happens during the **coding** stage on each module, as well as in the full testing stage once the program is complete.

front_blocks.md: What three things does the testing stage check?

back_blocks.md: That the program **meets all the original requirements**, **handles valid and invalid input correctly**, and **performs reliably under different conditions**.

cards.front_md: What three things does the testing stage check?
cards.back_md: That the program **meets all the original requirements**, **handles valid and invalid input correctly**, and **performs reliably under different conditions**.

front_blocks.md: When does the maintenance stage begin?

back_blocks.md: **After the program has been delivered** to the client or end users.

cards.front_md: When does the maintenance stage begin?
cards.back_md: **After the program has been delivered** to the client or end users.

front_blocks.md: Name three activities in the maintenance stage.

back_blocks.md: **Fixing bugs** that were not discovered during testing, **updating features** to meet new requirements, and **improving performance** or adapting to new systems.

cards.front_md: Name three activities in the maintenance stage.
cards.back_md: **Fixing bugs** that were not discovered during testing, **updating features** to meet new requirements, and **improving performance** or adapting to new systems.

front_blocks.md: Software maintenance ensures the program remains useful and <u>**                **</u> over time.

back_blocks.md: Software maintenance ensures the program remains useful and **reliable** over time.

cards.front_md: Software maintenance ensures the program remains useful and <u>**                **</u> over time.
cards.back_md: Software maintenance ensures the program remains useful and **reliable** over time.

front_blocks.md: Define **Waterfall model**.

back_blocks.md: The Waterfall model is a **sequential software development process divided into distinct phases**, where each phase must be completed before the next one begins.

cards.front_md: Define **Waterfall model**.
cards.back_md: The Waterfall model is a **sequential software development process divided into distinct phases**, where each phase must be completed before the next one begins.

front_blocks.md: The Waterfall model is a <u>**                    **</u> software development process.

back_blocks.md: The Waterfall model is a **sequential** software development process.

cards.front_md: The Waterfall model is a <u>**                    **</u> software development process.
cards.back_md: The Waterfall model is a **sequential** software development process.

front_blocks.md: Name the six phases of the Waterfall model.

back_blocks.md: **Requirement gathering and analysis**, **system design**, **implementation**, **integration and testing**, **deployment**, and **maintenance**.

cards.front_md: Name the six phases of the Waterfall model.
cards.back_md: **Requirement gathering and analysis**, **system design**, **implementation**, **integration and testing**, **deployment**, and **maintenance**.

front_blocks.md: What happens in the system design phase of the Waterfall model?

back_blocks.md: The requirements are **translated into a design**, defining the **overall architecture** and identifying the **main components**.

cards.front_md: What happens in the system design phase of the Waterfall model?
cards.back_md: The requirements are **translated into a design**, defining the **overall architecture** and identifying the **main components**.

front_blocks.md: What happens at deployment in the Waterfall model?

back_blocks.md: The product is **released or handed over to the client**, which may involve **installation, customisation and training**.

cards.front_md: What happens at deployment in the Waterfall model?
cards.back_md: The product is **released or handed over to the client**, which may involve **installation, customisation and training**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
In the Waterfall model, phases can overlap.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Each phase **must be completed before the next one begins**.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

In the Waterfall model, phases can overlap.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

Each phase **must be completed before the next one begins**.

front_blocks.md: Name two benefits of the Waterfall model.

back_blocks.md: It is **simple and linear**, it has **clear stages and milestones** so progress is easy to track, and it is **ideal for well-defined projects**.

cards.front_md: Name two benefits of the Waterfall model.
cards.back_md: It is **simple and linear**, it has **clear stages and milestones** so progress is easy to track, and it is **ideal for well-defined projects**.

front_blocks.md: Name two drawbacks of the Waterfall model.

back_blocks.md: It is **inflexible** once development begins, it is **expensive to fix late problems**, and it has a **long development cycle**.

cards.front_md: Name two drawbacks of the Waterfall model.
cards.back_md: It is **inflexible** once development begins, it is **expensive to fix late problems**, and it has a **long development cycle**.

front_blocks.md: When is the Waterfall model most suitable?

back_blocks.md: When **requirements are well understood and unlikely to change**, and where **high quality and compliance are essential**.

cards.front_md: When is the Waterfall model most suitable?
cards.back_md: When **requirements are well understood and unlikely to change**, and where **high quality and compliance are essential**.

front_blocks.md: Define **iterative model**.

back_blocks.md: The iterative model is a **type of Agile software development methodology** that promotes **adaptability and high customer involvement**.

cards.front_md: Define **iterative model**.
cards.back_md: The iterative model is a **type of Agile software development methodology** that promotes **adaptability and high customer involvement**.

front_blocks.md: Define **sprint**.

back_blocks.md: A sprint is a **short time-boxed development period**, usually 1 to 4 weeks.

cards.front_md: Define **sprint**.
cards.back_md: A sprint is a **short time-boxed development period**, usually 1 to 4 weeks.

front_blocks.md: How are requirements often written in the iterative model?

back_blocks.md: As **user stories**.

cards.front_md: How are requirements often written in the iterative model?
cards.back_md: As **user stories**.

front_blocks.md: What happens in a sprint review?

back_blocks.md: The working software is **demonstrated to stakeholders**, and **feedback is collected** to identify changes or improvements.

cards.front_md: What happens in a sprint review?
cards.back_md: The working software is **demonstrated to stakeholders**, and **feedback is collected** to identify changes or improvements.

front_blocks.md: What happens in a sprint retrospective?

back_blocks.md: The team **reflects on what went well and what needs improving**, focusing on **team performance and process optimisation**.

cards.front_md: What happens in a sprint retrospective?
cards.back_md: The team **reflects on what went well and what needs improving**, focusing on **team performance and process optimisation**.

front_blocks.md: How is testing handled in the iterative model?

back_blocks.md: Testing is **ongoing** throughout the sprint, not saved for the end.

cards.front_md: How is testing handled in the iterative model?
cards.back_md: Testing is **ongoing** throughout the sprint, not saved for the end.

front_blocks.md: Name two benefits of the iterative model.

back_blocks.md: It is **highly adaptable**, it promotes **frequent communication**, it **focuses on quality**, and it ensures **customer collaboration**.

cards.front_md: Name two benefits of the iterative model.
cards.back_md: It is **highly adaptable**, it promotes **frequent communication**, it **focuses on quality**, and it ensures **customer collaboration**.

front_blocks.md: Name two drawbacks of the iterative model.

back_blocks.md: It **requires experienced team members**, carries a **risk of burnout**, **may lack documentation**, and risks **scope creep**.

cards.front_md: Name two drawbacks of the iterative model.
cards.back_md: It **requires experienced team members**, carries a **risk of burnout**, **may lack documentation**, and risks **scope creep**.

front_blocks.md: When is the iterative model most suitable?

back_blocks.md: For **small to medium-sized projects** where **requirements can change** and customer involvement is high.

cards.front_md: When is the iterative model most suitable?
cards.back_md: For **small to medium-sized projects** where **requirements can change** and customer involvement is high.

front_blocks.md: Define **Rapid Application Development (RAD)**.

back_blocks.md: RAD is a software development methodology that **emphasises fast and iterative development**.

cards.front_md: Define **Rapid Application Development (RAD)**.
cards.back_md: RAD is a software development methodology that **emphasises fast and iterative development**.

front_blocks.md: Name the five steps of RAD.

back_blocks.md: **Requirement planning**, **user design and prototyping**, **construction or iterative development**, **cutover or deployment**, and **maintenance and updates**.

cards.front_md: Name the five steps of RAD.
cards.back_md: **Requirement planning**, **user design and prototyping**, **construction or iterative development**, **cutover or deployment**, and **maintenance and updates**.

front_blocks.md: What happens in the user design and prototyping step of RAD?

back_blocks.md: Developers **collaborate with users to develop prototypes**, ensuring alignment with user needs.

cards.front_md: What happens in the user design and prototyping step of RAD?
cards.back_md: Developers **collaborate with users to develop prototypes**, ensuring alignment with user needs.

front_blocks.md: What happens at cutover in RAD?

back_blocks.md: The product is **transitioned into the live environment**, including **user training, support and documentation**.

cards.front_md: What happens at cutover in RAD?
cards.back_md: The product is **transitioned into the live environment**, including **user training, support and documentation**.

front_blocks.md: Name two benefits of RAD.

back_blocks.md: **Speed** of development and delivery at relatively low cost, **user involvement**, **flexibility**, and **incremental development** in small testable parts.

cards.front_md: Name two benefits of RAD.
cards.back_md: **Speed** of development and delivery at relatively low cost, **user involvement**, **flexibility**, and **incremental development** in small testable parts.

front_blocks.md: Name two drawbacks of RAD.

back_blocks.md: It **requires strong team collaboration**, risks **quality issues** because speed may reduce testing and documentation, is **not ideal for small projects**, and carries a **scope creep risk**.

cards.front_md: Name two drawbacks of RAD.
cards.back_md: It **requires strong team collaboration**, risks **quality issues** because speed may reduce testing and documentation, is **not ideal for small projects**, and carries a **scope creep risk**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
RAD is best suited to small, simple projects.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
RAD is **not ideal for small projects**, because it may be **too complex for simple systems**.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

RAD is best suited to small, simple projects.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

RAD is **not ideal for small projects**, because it may be **too complex for simple systems**.

front_blocks.md: When is RAD most suitable?

back_blocks.md: When **rapid delivery is required** and where requirements can be **developed and refined on the go**.

cards.front_md: When is RAD most suitable?
cards.back_md: When **rapid delivery is required** and where requirements can be **developed and refined on the go**.

front_blocks.md: Both the iterative model and RAD carry a risk of <u>**          **</u> creep, where flexibility leads to ever-expanding requirements.

back_blocks.md: Both the iterative model and RAD carry a risk of **scope** creep, where flexibility leads to ever-expanding requirements.

cards.front_md: Both the iterative model and RAD carry a risk of <u>**          **</u> creep, where flexibility leads to ever-expanding requirements.
cards.back_md: Both the iterative model and RAD carry a risk of **scope** creep, where flexibility leads to ever-expanding requirements.
